ideas.description: Find the Muon knee below 7.5 epochs. On the tip E018 (commit d634e3b: Muon NS3, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, 7.5 epochs), change only the epoch count from 7.5 to 7.0. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. 7 epochs is a whole number, so the half-epoch permutation trick is not needed. The final partial batch shape stays the one compiled in build(). Nothing else changes.
ideas.expected: Accuracy 0.750-0.759, point estimate ~0.7555 (E018 0.7596 minus ~0.86 pp/epoch x 0.5). Time 6.80-7.05 s, point ~6.92 s (-6% vs 7.39 s). If feasible, this is a new best and gives a ~0.25 pp margin. Bank lr/tail gains before trying 6.5. If it is infeasible by less than 0.3 pp, keep the E018 tip and retry 7.0 after the lr 0.16 or the Muon lr floor change.

ideas.description: Systems change to the Muon optimizer step only; the recipe math stays the same. Muon currently costs 1.93 ms/step of GPU time (about 10% of the step), mostly as many small kernels: 9 per-param calls, each with momentum, norm and projection ops plus per-iteration NS elementwise work. Replace them with one torch.compile'd Muon step over all conv filters. Do the momentum and Nesterov update with torch._foreach_* ops. Stack same-shape flattened filters within each block (128x1152, 384x3456, 576x5184 pairs) and run the 3 quintic NS iterations as one bmm per shape group. Apply the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling and the weight-norm projection inside the same compiled function. Pass the Muon lr as a 0-d GPU tensor so schedule changes do not recompile. Compile and warm up in build() on synthetic tensors. Run the drafts/debug_nan.py one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching (E009 lesson). Measure the Muon step GPU time with drafts/time_muon.py before and after.
ideas.expected: Muon step GPU time drops from 1.93 ms to ~0.6-1.1 ms. Total time falls 3-6%, from 7.39 s to ~7.0-7.2 s (point ~7.12 s). Accuracy within ±0.25 pp (re-draw only; the math is identical). A gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1 and means Muon overhead was FLOP-bound, not launch-bound. Applies to whichever epoch count is the tip.

ideas.description: Pre-registered follow-up to E019 (Muon lr 0.36 cost 1.04 pp on every seed). On the current tip (the 7.0-epoch Muon run if it is kept, else E018 at 7.5 epochs), change only the Muon lr for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.16. The SGD lr for BN biases, whitening bias and head, the schedule shape, lookahead and NS3 all stay unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.5 pp, point +0.15 pp: E019 shows the optimum is at or below 0.24, but it may be flat between 0.16 and 0.24. Time unchanged (±1.5% jitter). A gain of 0.25 pp or more is real and buys ~0.3 epoch (~4% time at the knee); then try 0.12. A drop of 0.25 pp or more puts the optimum near 0.24 and closes the lr axis.

ideas.description: Lower the end-of-schedule floor for the Muon group only. E019's post-mortem says the Muon lr is an unbuffered per-step relative rotation, and the 0.07x terminal floor leaves end-of-training noise that lookahead cannot average out. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier so it decays linearly to 0 at the final step instead of to 0.07x. The warmup and the rest of the decay keep the same shape. The SGD group (BN biases, head) keeps its existing schedule, including its 0.07x floor. Lookahead is unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp, point +0.15 pp, at unchanged time (±1.5%). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.2 for the Muon group and stacks with the lr 0.16 result to allow ~0.25-0.5 fewer epochs. A drop of 0.15 pp or more (as with SGD's decay-to-zero in E012) means the floor helps; then leave the tail alone.

ideas.description: Explore Muon momentum, inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon at bs ~2000. On the current tip, change only the Muon Nesterov momentum from 0.6 to 0.8. Muon lr, NS3, lookahead and the SGD group stay the same. Rationale: at bs 1024 with a 100-way head, per-step gradients are noisier than in the bs-2000 CIFAR-10 setting. Heavier momentum averages more before orthogonalization, which normalizes away gradient magnitude, so momentum is the only knob that filters direction noise.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp. Time unchanged. A gain of 0.25 pp or more opens a momentum axis (try 0.9). A loss of 0.25 pp or more suggests 0.6 or lower is right (try 0.45 only if the lr 0.16 result also points toward less aggressive updates).

ideas.description: Explore the D003 mechanism (C0016/C0017): how a 4D kernel is split before orthogonalization. Replace the flattened [out, in*9] orthogonalization with a real frequency-wise variant of Muon-C. Project each 3x3 kernel momentum onto an orthonormal real 3x3 basis (the tensor product of the 3-point orthonormal DCT-II), which gives 9 [out, in] matrices per layer. Orthogonalize them with one batched 3-step NS (bmm over the 9 frequencies), then transform back to the spatial domain. The output scaling uses sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the [out,in] shape. Keep the weight-norm projection, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead and the epoch count of the current tip. Compile in build() and run the one-step finite-gradient check first.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.5 to +0.6 pp, point +0.15 pp (C0017 reports a stronger early trajectory, which is what counts at 7-7.5 epochs, but this lr was tuned for flattened Muon). Time +0 to +3%: the NS FLOPs are similar, with 9 small bmm groups instead of one wide matrix. A gain of 0.4 pp or more is worth ~0.5 epoch and makes the frequency split the new Muon base. A loss of 0.3 pp or more closes the kernel-split branch.

drop.reason: Its base (the Muon 8-epoch run) is no longer the tip: E018 runs 7.5 epochs. The trade is also known to lose. E013 measured low-res epochs at ~0.058 pp per 1% time, while cutting epochs on Muon costs ~0.13 pp per 1% (0.86 pp for ~6.7% time per epoch, E018). Spending accuracy on 24 px epochs is therefore about 2x worse than dropping whole epochs. Expected outcome: break-even at best.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E018: Muon with 3 Newton-Schulz steps, lookahead, 7.5 epochs, accuracy 0.7596, 7.39 s, a 0.66 pp margin over 0.753. The new ideas cash that margin in.

**Exploit**
- **7.0 epochs (priority 5):** expected ~0.7555 at ~6.9 s.
- **One compiled, batched Muon step (priority 4):** targets the 1.93 ms/step of Muon kernel overhead; expect -3% to -6% time with the math unchanged. It is tagged H2.4 and also tests whether H2's "not optimizer overhead" claim still holds now that the optimizer is heavier.
- **Muon lr 0.16 (priority 4):** the follow-up E019 pre-registered.
- **Muon terminal lr decaying to 0 instead of 0.07x (priority 3):** for the Muon group only, tests H1.6.2. The E019 post-mortem points to the lr floor as end-of-run noise.

**Explore**
- **Muon momentum 0.6 → 0.8 (priority 2).**
- **Frequency-wise (DCT-basis) Muon-C kernel split (priority 2):** from D003 C0016/C0017.

I023 (GELU → SiLU) stays queued. I022 (Muon without lookahead) is still running; its result decides whether averaging-density ideas (H1.6.1) are worth queuing on the Muon base, so none were added yet.

I dropped I024: progressive resizing buys time at about half the accuracy-per-time rate of cutting Muon epochs.

That leaves 7 queued ideas.

**Stale hypotheses:** H1.1.4 (SGD at 8.75 epochs) and H1.5.1 width-for-epochs now concern the superseded SGD base. They should be re-scoped to the Muon base or retired at the next tree review.
